documentNotes.title: Dear iGEO participant,
documentNotes.statement:
Before starting your virtual trip of the Sariyer district of Istanbul city, please read these guidelines.

1. You have the printed Map of the FWE-I area. Use this map to orient yourself and find the location of five topical sites. The sites are marked on the map, but not labelled.
2. The sequence of moving from one site to another is in numeric order: Site 1 (Start) → Site 2 → Site 3 → Site 4 → Site 5 (Finish).
3. The absolute height (elevation) at each site is lower than of the previous one on the route. Always go down!
4. “Leaving” one site and “arriving” at the next one, do not return. Always move forward!
5. At each site you will get tasks you need to complete. For FWE-I you can gain maximum **15 marks**.
6. You are to decide for how long you will be “staying” at each site.
7. Answers should be written in English on the Response Sheet. For answers use a pen with a dark blue tint only. Do not forget to write your participant code in the upper right corner of both pages of the Response Sheet.
8. This presentation will be stopped when **60 minutes** end, regardless of whether you have visited all five sites, or not. Deliver your Response Sheet to the supervisor of your exam immediately then.
9. Keep the Map with you, it can be used as reference for Part II of the Fieldwork exercise (FWE-II).

**Good luck!**

transcription.notes: Digital slide deck (14 landscape slides), fully legible; no illegible spots. No official solutions or marking scheme in the archive, so every problem has solution.incomplete and no answer. Points: only the total is printed ("maximum 15 marks", guideline 5); no per-site or per-part points are printed, so all points are null. Time limit 60 minutes from guideline 8. round kept as the catalogue code "experiment" (the masthead reads "Fieldwork Exercise Part I"); roundType set to practical for a fieldwork exercise. Structure: 6 top-level problems (Sites 1-5 plus the Concluding question) with 14 labelled parts (1.A-1.B, 2.A-2.B, 3.A-3.D, 4.A-4.C, 5.A-5.C); the catalogue's ~15 presumably counts the unlabelled bulleted Concluding question, which is kept in the statement of problem 6 because it has no label. Guidelines slide (page 2) and authors/sources slide (page 14) are in paper.documentNotes; in the guidelines, items "6.You", "8.This", "9.Keep" are printed without a space after the number — a space was added for list formatting. Page 3 ("ARRIVING TO THE STARTING POINT") is put at the start of problem 1; its text is printed over the Istanbul railway network map, so the map crop p1-fig1 is the whole slide and contains that overlaid text. Printed source errors kept verbatim: "Imagine you to the Hacıosman metro station" (missing verb, page 3); "lower than of the previous one" (page 2); "Julgans regia" for Juglans regia in the photo label E (page 7, inside the figure; the credits on page 14 spell it Juglans); "give their origin" for a single rock (3.D, page 8); "figures 3.A.-3.F." while the rock photos are labelled A.-F. under "Figure 3. Rocks" (page 9); "options for make it closer to the hypothetic number" (4.C, page 10); "Mikhail Drugov Natalia Frolova" without comma (page 14); on page 13 the captions are numbered "Fig. 1a" and "Fig. 2b" (inconsistent in the source); "Lensoidal" and "Rocks names" in the chronostratigraphic chart (page 8). Chronostratigraphic chart (page 8) rendered as a Markdown table: merged cells (Devonian spanning two rows, Ordovician spanning three rows, the empty Series cell of layer 3) are given once in the first row with blank cells below; the header cells "Middle / -Upper" and "Lower- / Middle" are printed on two lines and joined as "Middle-Upper" and "Lower-Middle"; entry 1 is italic as printed. The rock photos (Figure 3) and species photos (2.B) carry their labels inside the crops. The text layer contains a stray invisible string "Hh hhh" on page 13 that is not visible on the rendered slide and was not transcribed. Rule-16 classification fields were not written (no classification sidecar requested in this pilot).

problems.title: SITE 1. ISTANBUL HEIGHTS
problems.statement:
**ARRIVING TO THE STARTING POINT**

Imagine you to the **Hacıosman** metro station (**green line**), located in the Eastern Thrace, 2 km from the Bosphorus.

**Site 1** is right across the road from an unfinished building of a hotel.

Analyze the map extract and assuming that each floor of this building is 2.5 meters in height and the terrace on its roof is the same height, answer the questions from the next slide.

figures.caption: İstanbul Raylı Sistemler Ağ Haritası / Istanbul Railway Network Map
figures.alt: Istanbul railway network map (Metro Istanbul, 2021) covering the whole slide: coloured metro, tram, funicular and suburban lines on both sides of the Bosphorus, with the green M2 line running north to its terminus Hacıosman; legends “Mevcut Hatlar / Lines In Operation”, “Yapımı Devam Eden Hatlar / Lines Under Construction”, “İşaretler / Signs”, “Bilgilendirme / Information”, “İletişim / Contact”. The task text “ARRIVING TO THE STARTING POINT …” is printed over the top-left corner of the map.

Topographic map extract with contour lines (labels 90, 110, 120), green forest areas, orange main roads (Hacı Osman Bayırı Caddesi, Tarabya Bayırı Caddesi, Büyükdere Caddesi) and a junction; a star marks Site 1 just west of the Hacıosman metro station (M symbol); street names Dönence Sokağı, Zambak Sokağı, Çamlık Caddesi and others in the north-east; scale bar 100 m in the lower-left corner.

figures.caption: Fig. 1a. Hotel building near Site 1.
figures.alt: Photo of a tall unfinished concrete high-rise building (bare floors, no facade) beside a road with grass and trees in the foreground.

figures.caption: Fig. 1b. The 15 July Martyrs Bridge.
figures.alt: Photo of a suspension bridge over the Bosphorus with a ferry in the foreground; a red double-headed arrow beside a pylon is labelled “165 m.”.

figures.caption: Fig.1c. The Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge.
figures.alt: Photo of a suspension bridge spanning the Bosphorus between wooded shores; a red double-headed arrow beside the pylon is labelled “105 m.”.

figures.caption: Fig.1d. The Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge.
figures.alt: Photo of a cable-stayed bridge with tall A-shaped pylons under a blue sky; a red double-headed arrow beside the nearer pylon is labelled “322 m.”.

parts.label: 1.A.
parts.statement: Is the absolute height (elevation) of the hotel building higher than pillars of bridges over The Bosphorus strait?

parts.label: 1.B.
parts.statement: Estimate the difference (in meters) of the height of this building and the pillars of the highest bridge over The Bosphorus.

problems.statementAfterParts: Write your answers on the Response Sheet and move to the next site.

problems.title: SITE 2 – MEDITERRANEAN VEGETATION
problems.statement:
**Site 2** is in the middle of the Ataturk urban forest, established in 2021. This is a park with native and planted trees, developed on the unbuilt area in Sariyer district.

Be an expert in Mediterranean vegetation and answer the questions 2.A. (this slide) and 2.B. (next slide).

figures.alt: Photo of dense mixed forest in the Ataturk urban forest: tall pines at the back, broadleaf trees and shrubs overgrown with climbers in front.

parts.label: 2.A.
parts.statement: The Mediterranean forests, woodlands and shrubs biome is spread worldwide. Provide the common names of five different Mediterranean types of vegetation and specify the continents where each of these types is represented.

parts.label: 2.B.
parts.statement: Select the species from the photos which are NOT native for the forests of modern Istanbul city area and write down on the Response Sheet the corresponding letter codes (A-F).

figures.alt: Grid of six plant photos with labels: A. Quercus frainetto (lobed oak leaves with acorns); B. Pinus brutia (pine branch with needles and cones); C. Ficus carica (fig leaves with green fruits); D. Acer mandshuricum (compound leaves with serrated leaflets); E. Julgans regia (walnut leaves with a splitting green husk); F. Araucaria araucana (spiny scale-leaved branches).

problems.statementAfterParts: Write your answers on the Response Sheet and move to the next site.

problems.title: SITE 3 – GEOLOGY OF EASTERN THRACE

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Site 3.
figures.alt: Photo of a path curving along a hillside cut with an exposed reddish-brown rock face, street lamps, a red-leaved shrub, grass and pine trees above.

figures.caption: Fig. 2. Rock outcrop at Site 3.
figures.alt: Close-up photo of a fractured reddish-brown to pinkish rock outcrop with tilted, blocky layers.

figures.caption: Figure 3. Rocks
figures.alt: Grid of six rock-specimen photos, each with a 1 cm scale bar, labelled A.–F.: A. rock with rounded dark pebbles in a light sandy matrix; B. dark grey-green foliated rock; C. light grey-beige granular rock; D. rock packed with fossil shells and pebbles; E. greenish-grey banded foliated rock with rusty spots; F. dark fine-grained rock. Small round thin-section images appear in some panels.

parts.label: 3.A.
parts.statement: Identify the exposed rock and its origin.

parts.label: 3.B.
parts.statement:
The chronostratigraphic chart below contains the results from drilling a geological borehole here. Which geological system (period) name is omitted in Column 1?

**Chronostratigraphic chart**

| System/ Period | Series/ Epoch | Rocks names |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Devonian | Middle-Upper | 1. *The rock from photo on figure 2* |
|  | Lower-Middle | 2. Shales with calciturbidite intercalations |
| ? |  | 3. Limestones (biogenic) |
| Ordovician | Middle | 4. Laminated grey shales with quartz arenite lenses |
|  | Middle | 5. Quartz arenites |
|  | Lower | 6. Lensoidal conglomerates- sandstone shale |

parts.label: 3.C.
parts.statement: Match the rocks, shown on figures 3.A.-3.F. of the next slide, to the layers 2-6 in the Chronostratigraphic chart.

parts.label: 3.D.
parts.statement: Identify the rock from the Figure 3 NOT found in this borehole and give their origin.

problems.title: SITE 4 – RIVER
problems.statement:
**Site 4** is located on the dam over a small river running through the Ataturk urban forest.

Consult the map extract on the next page and circle on the printed map the catchment area of this river.

figures.caption: Fig.1. Dam on the river in the Ataturk urban forest.
figures.alt: Photo of a small pond held by a dam, green water surrounded by dense trees, a small stone structure in the water and a muddy bank in the foreground.

figures.caption: Fig.2. Mean annual river runoff (surface runoff) near Bosphorus, mm.
figures.alt: Fragment of a small-scale runoff map around the Bosphorus with isolines labelled 100, 30, 300, 200, 500 and 300; Russian place names „Эргене“ and „Стамбул“ with the overlaid label “Istanbul”.

Topographic map extract of the Ataturk urban forest (green area) bounded by orange main roads (Tarabya Bayırı Caddesi, Hacı Osman Bayırı Caddesi) with contour lines, black paths, a small blue pond in the middle and a blue reservoir with a dam in the south-east; five stars mark sites along the route from the north (near Hacıosman) to the south-east; scale bar 100 m in the lower-left corner.

parts.label: 4.A.
parts.statement: Estimate the annual runoff of this river ($\mathrm{m^3}$).

parts.label: 4.B.
parts.statement: In urban households equipped with water pipe and sanitation systems, the water consumption norm per capita is 150 liters. How many people could hypothetically get all the water they need from this river? (provide a number)

parts.label: 4.C.
parts.statement: Why in real life, is this number much lower, and what are the options for make it closer to the hypothetic number?

problems.statementAfterParts: Write your answers on the Response Sheet and move to the next site.

problems.title: SITE 5 – BUILDING ON SLOPES
problems.statement: **Site 5** corresponds to the spot marked with ‘X’ on the map extract in the Response Sheet.

figures.caption: Fig.1. Housing near Site 5.
figures.alt: Photo of multi-storey houses densely built on a steep wooded hillside above a newly paved park area with young trees and workers.

figures.caption: Fig.2.
figures.alt: First quadrant of the unit circle on x–y axes: points (1, 0), (√3/2, 1/2), (√2/2, √2/2), (1/2, √3/2) and (0, 1) on the arc, with rays for angles 0°/0, 30°/π/6, 45°/π/4, 60°/π/3 and 90°/π/2.

parts.label: 5.A.
parts.statement: Mark Spot ‘Y’ on this fragment, which is located 40 meters from Spot X on a bearing of 60 degrees (in azimuth 60 degrees).

parts.label: 5.B.
parts.statement: Estimate the steepness of the slope (inclination angle in degrees) between spots X and Y.

parts.label: 5.C.
parts.statement:
Which types of mass wasting (slope movement) represent danger for building on slopes with similar steepness near the Ataturk Urban Forest:

*a) avalanche, b) creep, c) lahar,*  
*d) landslide, e) rock-fall, f) solifluction?*

problems.title: CONCLUDING QUESTION
problems.statement:
Near the Ataturk urban forest several traditional rural style houses can be found. Until 1937, there was a settlement here, named *Çamlıtepe Village*.

- Which features of this geographical location have benefited the development of this settlement?

figures.caption: Fig. 1a. Historical photo of Çamlıtepe Village
figures.alt: Old sepia photograph of a village street with stone and tiled-roof houses, a mosque with a minaret, people and a horse cart, and a bare hillside behind.

figures.caption: Fig. 2b. Old country style house (slum) near the park
figures.alt: Colour photo of a hillside with an old tiled-roof house in the foreground among trees and colourful multi-storey apartment buildings behind under a blue sky.
